FOREWORD This Indian Standard was adopted by the Bureau of Indian Standards, atler the draft finalized by the Pesticides and Pesticides Residue Analysis Sectional Committee had been approved by the Food and Agriculture Division Council. Metsulfhron methyl, technical is employed in the preparation of herbicidal formulations for agricultural use. Metsulfuron methyl is the accepted common name by the International Organization for Standardization (ISO) for Methyl 2-[[[[(4-methoxy-6 -methyl-l ,3,5 -triazin-2-yl) amino] carbonyl]amino] sulfonyl]benzoate. The empirical and structural formulae and the molecular mass of metsulfuron methyl are given below:
Empirical Formula Structural Formula Molecular Mass

381.37

In preparation of this standard, due consideration has been given to the provisions of the Insecticides Act, 1968 and the Rules framed thereunder. However, this standard is subject to the restrictions imposed under the Insecticides Act and Rules, wherever applicable. For the purpose of deciding whether a particular requirement of this standard is complied with the final value, observed or calculated, expressing the result of a test or analysis, shall be rounded off in accordance with IS 2:1960 `Rules for rounding off numerical values (revised)'. The number of significant places retained in the rcumded off value should be the same as that of the specified value in this standard.

ANNEX

A

[Table 1, Item (i)]
DETERMINATION OF METSULFURON METHYL CONTENT

A-1 PRINCIPLE Metsulfuron methyl content is determined by high performance liquid chromatography (HPLC) using internal standard technique. A-2 APPARATUS A-2.1 A high performance liquid chromatography system coupled with ultraviolet detector and a printerplotter-turn-integrator is used for this determination. The suggested operative parameters are as follows, but can be changed if necessary, provided standardization is done. Column : Reverse phase C8, Cl 8 or equivalent pre-packed column, 150 mm x 4.6 mm, with a 5 v in-line filter (Filter required to protect the analytical column) Temperature : Ambient temperature Mobile phase : Acetonitrile: Water (35 :65, v/v), pH = 3.0 adjusted with 85 percent phosphoric acid (H,POJ Flow rate : 2.0 ml/min Injection vol. : 20 microlitre Detector : ultraviolet detector (254 nm)
Balance

A-3 REAGENTS A-3.1 Acetonitrile, HPLC/AR grade. A-3.2 Water, HPLC/AR grade." A-3.3 Phosphoric Acid, I+PLC/AR grade, 85 percent. A-3.4 Ammonium Hydroxide, ARgrade, 30.0 percent. A-3.5 Phenyl Sulfone, purity AR grade. internal standard, of known analytical reference

Methyl, A-3.6 Metsulfuron standard, of known purity.

A-4 PROCEDURE A-4.1 Preparation
of Internal Standard

Weigh 9.0 g of phenyl sulfone in a 1000 ml volumetric flask and make up to volume with acetonitrile. Dissolve ultrasonically for about 10 min and equilibrate the solution for half an hour to room temperature. A-4.2 Preparation
of Make-up Phase

Pipette 0.8 ml of concentrated 30 percent ammonium hydroxide (15N NHqOH) into 1 litre of water, thus making a 0.0 IN NHAOH.Add 1 litre of acetonitrile to prepare the 50/50 make-up phase. A-4.3 Preparation
of Standard Solution

A-2.2 Analytical
A-2.3 pH Meter

A-2.4 Microlitre

Syringe, 25 microlitre.

Bath

A-2.7 Standard Glassware
`7 .

Weigh accurately 100 mg of metsulfuron methyl analytical standard into a 100 ml volumetric flask. Pipette 10 ml of phenyl sulfone internal standard solution and make it to volume with sample solvent. Ultrascmicate.for 15-reinto dissolve completely. Label flask as standard solution.

B IS is a statutory institution established under the Bureau of Indian Standards Act, 1986 to promote harmonious development of the activities of standardization, marking and quality certification of goods and attending to connected matters in the country.

Review of Indian Standards

Amendments are issued to standards as the need arises on the basis of comments. Standards are also reviewed periodically; a standard along with amendments is reaffirmed when such review indicates that no changes are needed; if the review indicates that changes are needed, it is taken up for revision. Users of Indian Standards should ascertain that they are in possession of the latest amendments or edition by referring to the latest issue of `BIS Catalogue' and `Standards : Monthly Additions'. This Indian Standard has been developed from Doc : No. FAD 1 (1348).
